title: Mental Health Therapy Office Rates: What Counseling Practice Janitorial Service Costs
seoTitle: Mental Health Therapy Office Rates: Counseling Practice Cleaning Cost
metaDescription: Mental health therapy office rates average $0.09–$0.20/sq ft per visit, about $1,400–$7,800/month for 1,200–3,600 sq ft. Estimate yours in our calculator.
excerpt: Therapy and counseling practices are among the lighter-soil healthcare tenants, but quiet scheduling, carpeted session rooms, and patient privacy shape how they are priced. Here are per-sq-ft rates, monthly budgets by practice size, and the right weekly frequency.
quickAnswer: Therapy and counseling practices typically pay $0.12–$0.20 per sq ft per visit under 2,500 sq ft and $0.09–$0.15 per sq ft per visit from 2,500 to 9,999 sq ft, plus $15–$30 per restroom. A 1,200 sq ft solo or two-clinician suite cleaned twice a week runs about $1,400–$2,300 per month, while a 3,600 sq ft group practice cleaned three times a week runs roughly $4,600–$7,800. Most practices do well with two or three visits a week rather than nightly service.

blocks.text: How Therapy Practices Differ From Other Healthcare Tenants

A counseling or psychotherapy practice sits at the low-soil end of healthcare cleaning. There are no procedures, no blood exposure in normal operations, and no exam tables. What there is: a waiting room, a cluster of 120 to 180 sq ft session rooms with upholstered seating, a few clinician offices, a small staff kitchen, and one or two restrooms shared by clients and staff. Patient throughput is moderate, often one client per clinician per hour, so a six-clinician group sees 30 to 40 clients a day spread across long appointment blocks.

That profile means therapy suites price close to professional office space rather than clinical space. The adjustments come from three places: carpet and upholstered furniture that need more vacuuming attention than open-plan desks, high tissue and waste volume in every session room, and restrooms that serve the public. Vendors also account for scheduling constraints, because many practices see evening clients until 8 or 9 p.m., which pushes cleaning into late-night windows.

blocks.text: Therapy practices usually land in the lower half of each band because session rooms are low-soil and a crew can clean a 150 sq ft room in 4 to 6 minutes. Practices with mixed flooring, where waiting and corridors are LVT and session rooms are carpet, pay about 5 percent more than all-carpet suites because crews need both vacuum and damp mop setups.

Monthly pricing equals per-visit price times visits per month at 4.33 weeks per month. Weekly service is 4.33 visits, twice weekly is 8.66, and three times weekly is 13. Lower frequencies carry a higher per-visit multiplier because each visit handles more accumulated soil, so weekly service costs about 8 percent more per visit than the twice-weekly baseline.

blocks.title: Watch the 2,500 sq ft threshold
blocks.text: A 2,400 sq ft practice prices in the higher under-2,500 band, so its per-visit cost can approach that of a 3,600 sq ft practice. If your lease is close to the line, ask vendors to measure cleanable area and exclude storage and mechanical rooms.

Most therapy suites have one restroom per 1,500 to 2,000 sq ft, lower than medical clinics but higher than open-plan offices. Because clients often use the restroom before or after a session, it sees steady use all day. Supply run-outs are the most frequent complaint in counseling practices: a client who finds no toilet tissue or towels before an emotionally difficult session remembers it. High-capacity dispensers reduce that risk between visits.

items: Waiting room: upholstered seating collects lint and crumbs; vacuum cushions weekly and spot-clean fabric monthly.
Session rooms: tissue use is heavy; every room needs trash emptied on every visit, plus vacuuming and disinfecting door handles, lamp switches, and side tables.
Carpet traffic lanes: corridors between waiting room and session rooms show wear first; plan quarterly extraction at $0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month amortized.
Group therapy room: 8 to 12 chairs and higher soil; clean after each group day, not just on the regular schedule.
Staff kitchen: coffee and lunch in a small space; add breakroom sanitation at $12 to $25 per visit.

blocks.text: Two visits a week suits most solo and small group practices under 2,500 sq ft. Three visits a week fits group practices with 8 or more clinicians, evening hours, or a busy group therapy schedule. Five nights a week is warranted only for outpatient behavioral health centers with medication management, intake assessments, or partial hospitalization programs where foot traffic is high and some clients may be in crisis.

items.name: Count client visits per week
items.text: Under 80 client visits per week usually supports twice-weekly service; 80 to 200 visits points to three times weekly.

items.name: Match visits to your heaviest days
items.text: Schedule cleaning the night after your busiest client days, often Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday for evening-heavy practices.

items.name: Add a mid-week restroom check if needed
items.text: A short restroom-and-trash visit can cost less than a full additional clean while preventing supply run-outs.

items.name: Keep cleaning out of session hours
items.text: Vacuum noise and crews in hallways break confidentiality and calm; require service after the last client leaves.

blocks.text: Therapy offices do not need heavy clinical chemistry for routine cleaning. A plant-based EPA Safer Choice cleaner such as ECOS Pro Orange Plus handles side tables, desks, and counters with low VOCs, which matters in small, closed session rooms where scented products can bother clients. In restrooms, a Tork Twin Jumbo T2 tissue dispenser holds two 9-inch jumbo rolls with stub-roll use and a keyed lock, so tissue lasts between twice-weekly visits. A Georgia-Pacific enMotion 10-inch touchless towel dispenser runs whisper-quiet, which matters when restrooms share walls with session rooms, and it meets ADA depth limits.

blocks.title: Buy your own paper if you clean twice a week
blocks.text: Consumables included in the contract add $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit. For low-frequency practices, buying paper and soap directly and having the crew restock it is often cheaper and avoids supply gaps.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to clean a small therapy office?
faqs.a: A 900 to 1,200 sq ft practice with one restroom typically pays $570 to $970 per month for weekly cleaning and $1,060 to $2,340 per month for twice-weekly service at national average rates. Very small suites often hit the $90 to $135 per-visit minimum.

faqs.q: Do therapy practices need medical-grade cleaning?
faqs.a: Usually not. Routine counseling work does not involve blood exposure, so a standard commercial crew using EPA-registered disinfectant on restrooms and high-touch points is enough. Clinics that administer injections or collect specimens should add bloodborne pathogens training to the vendor requirements.

faqs.q: How often should a counseling practice be cleaned?
faqs.a: Two visits per week works for most practices under 2,500 sq ft. Group practices with eight or more clinicians, evening hours, or group therapy rooms usually need three visits per week, which equals 13 visits per month at 4.33 weeks per month.

faqs.q: Should the cleaning crew work while clients are in session?
faqs.a: No. Vacuum noise and staff in hallways can compromise confidentiality and disrupt sessions. Schedule service after the last appointment, and if your practice runs until 9 p.m., confirm the vendor can staff a late window without a surcharge.

faqs.q: What is usually excluded from a therapy office cleaning contract?
faqs.a: Carpet hot-water extraction, upholstery shampooing, window exteriors, and interior glass are often priced separately. Shredding bins and any files are always excluded. Ask vendors to list exclusions so bids can be compared on equal terms.
